memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Olive oil for the light; spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense; and onyx stones and other gems to be mounted on the ephod and breastpiece.'" - Exod 35:8-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The list keeps going, and it is worth noticing what sits side by side in it.

Olive oil — the most ordinary substance in an Israelite kitchen. Onyx stones and precious gems — rare, costly, the kind of thing a family might own one of. Both appear in the same breath, both requested by God, both essential to the tabernacle.

The oil kept the lamp burning. The gems were mounted on the high priest's breastpiece, where the names of the tribes were carried into God's presence. Neither could substitute for the other.

God's work has always been built this way. Some contributions are visible and impressive; most are not. The oil in the lamp was consumed and forgotten, replaced week after week by someone whose name we will never know. But without it, the light went out.

Paul makes the same point about the church: the parts of the body that seem weaker are indispensable (1 Cor 12:22). The person who quietly sets up chairs, prays at home, or cooks for a grieving family is not doing lesser work.

If your contribution feels ordinary, remember the olive oil. God asked for it by name.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you undervalue the contribution you are able to make?
2. Whose quiet, unseen service in your church have you overlooked?
3. Are you offering God the ordinary as readily as the impressive?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, whether my offering is precious or plain, receive it. Help me value the unseen work that keeps Your light burning. Amen.
